children: The 1.1% drop in German industrial output in July defies the solid order intake and noticeable recent improvement in business sentiment, KfW chief economist Dirk Schumacher says. "The decline in industrial production can therefore be explained primarily by production changes in the automotive industry," he says. German data agency Destatis noted that a multi-week shutdown at a car plant was likely one of the main drivers of the fall. In August and September, the low water levels of the Rhine likely further dampened production, Schumacher says. However, the signals from orders and sentiment indicators point to the underlying improving trend, even if that will probably only be reflected in the figures for the fourth quarter, he says.
